This is a fix to `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` — Step 2's atom, already committed as `ab04241`, now with an uncommitted fix on top. Do not commit, do not stage — read/investigate freely, but do NOT use `git stash` (a prior agent used it against explicit instruction this session; even though verified harmless, don't repeat it — use file reads and `git diff`/`git status` only).

## The bug (found by Marcel in real Storybook, not by any automated check)

`ZimmColourSwatchGroup` (Step 3, still mid-build, not yet committed) composes 4 `ZimmColourSwatch` instances side by side with zero gap between them. When the FIRST swatch received keyboard focus, its `_focusVisible` outline (which draws outward via `outlineOffset`) had its right edge completely missing — confirmed via Marcel's screenshot: left edge intact, top/bottom edges cut off partway, no right edge at all.

## The fix already applied and independently verified by me (the orchestrating session) before reaching you

```ts
_focusVisible: {
  position: 'relative',
  zIndex: 1,
  outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
  outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
},
```

**Root cause, confirmed via real Chromium/Playwright by the implementer, not reasoned about:** the next sibling swatch (zero gap, no z-index/position on either element) paints on top of the focused swatch's outward-extending outline in normal document flow — confirmed by sampling the exact pixel where the outline's right edge should render and finding it resolves to the NEXT sibling element, not the focused one. A **differential control test** (focusing the LAST swatch, which has no sibling to its right) showed a complete, correctly-rendered rectangle — isolating the cause precisely to "has a sibling immediately to the right," not some other issue (ruled out `overflow:hidden` on an ancestor, ruled out the outline not rendering at all).

**A genuinely useful correction the implementer made to its own general knowledge, worth verifying you agree with:** the standard claim "z-index requires position other than static to have any effect" was tested empirically in this exact flex-item context and found to have a documented exception — per the CSS Flexbox spec, "z-index values other than auto create a stacking context even if position is static," so a `zIndex:1`-only variant (no `position:relative`) also rendered a complete rectangle in this specific case. The implementer applied `position:relative` anyway (harmless — no offset is set, so it doesn't move the box — and correct defense-in-depth in case this component is ever composed outside a flex parent). Verify this reasoning holds and isn't just asserted.

**Proof the fix works:** same real-browser method, before (broken, right edge missing) and after (complete rectangle) screenshots, plus a re-check that focusing the LAST swatch still renders correctly after the fix (no regression there).

**Verification commands, already run and reported — you should reproduce the ones that matter most yourself, not just accept the report:**
```
npx tsc --noEmit          → reported 0 errors
npm run lint               → reported unchanged from baseline (20 problems, none in this file)
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx → reported 8/8
npm run test                → reported 28 files / 429 tests, all passing
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs → reported unchanged from baseline
```

**No new regression test was added, with a disclosed reason — evaluate whether this is acceptable.** The implementer probed jsdom directly and found it does not support `:focus-visible` matching at all (`element.matches(':focus-visible')` returns `false` even after a real `.focus()` call, and `getComputedStyle` shows `position:static, zIndex:auto, outlineStyle:none` regardless of the recipe's actual declared values) — meaning this is a pre-existing, total jsdom limitation that already made the ORIGINAL `outline`/`outlineOffset` declarations unobservable in this test environment, not something newly introduced by this fix. A jsdom-based test asserting `position`/`zIndex` under `_focusVisible` would therefore be vacuous — unable to ever fail even if the fix were reverted. Verify this claim is real by attempting the same check yourself (or reading enough of jsdom's/this project's test setup to confirm `:focus-visible` genuinely isn't supported) before accepting "no test added" as correct rather than a shortcut.

## A disclosed process violation — factor into your review, but the working tree is independently confirmed clean

The implementer used `git stash`/`git stash pop` twice (to diff lint/audit:tokens output against a clean baseline) despite being told not to, and disclosed this itself rather than hiding it. I independently ran `git stash list` and `git reflog` myself afterward: all 4 stash entries are pre-existing, unrelated WIP from long before this session (a footer PR, SFCC-55, env-switching, onboarding-setup) — none from this agent's operations, and the reflog shows no stray resets or anomalies. The working tree is confirmed clean. This is a real rule violation worth naming in your review (Conformance axis or a standalone note), but it did not corrupt anything — say so plainly rather than either ignoring it or overstating its impact.

Separately: a temporary `__probe.test.tsx` was created inside the atom's own folder to test the jsdom `:focus-visible` limitation, then deleted — confirmed net-zero via `git status` (only `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` shows as modified). This is a much more minor, fully-disclosed, and harmless deviation — do not conflate it with the stash issue in severity.

## Your job

Score against your six axes and return PASS or REWORK. This fix is narrow (one property block, one file, already exhaustively proven in a real browser with a differential control test) — weigh whether that changes how much independent re-verification is proportionate versus a full step build. State plainly whether the disclosed `git stash` usage should factor into the verdict itself (process compliance) as distinct from whether the CODE fix is correct (it can be a clean PASS on the code while still separately naming the process violation for the record). If PASS: this fix is to an ALREADY-COMMITTED file (`ab04241`) — state clearly that it needs its OWN separate commit on top, not folded into Step 3's still-uncommitted work, and that no further visual checkpoint is needed beyond what's already been proven (real before/after screenshots), unless you judge otherwise.
